rulings.challenge_claim: The case-report/person-shift boundary is well warranted and the hiphil-verb antithesis with the preceding row is correctly disclosed, but the row omits that its own closing verse carries a hevel-family evaluative tag, the same refrain-tag construction sibling row p02-004 discloses two rows earlier in this cluster.
rulings.grounds: Byte tier, independently re-derived from verse_map_oshb.json word splits: oshb:Eccl.6.2 -- this row's OWN closing verse -- carries זֶ֥ה הֶ֛בֶל ("this is vanity"), verse-final before וָחֳלִ֥י רָ֖ע הֽוּא ("and it is an evil affliction"). eccl_device_inventory.json hevel_refrain.attested_forms lists Eccl.6.2 under the bare הבל form, and by_chapter.6 = 5 names this verse among the chapter's five sites. Neither device_notes nor observed_substrate_signals mentions it -- the row's own observed_substrate_signals cites only the tachat_hashemesh entry for oshb:Eccl.6.1, leaving this row's OWN hevel site unnamed, unlike sibling row p02-004's explicit disclosure of its own hevel site at oshb:Eccl.5.9. The case-report/person-shift boundary warrant itself is a separate question (see the convergent OL item on this same row); this finding stands on its own as a completeness gap in the row's own device sweep.
rulings.remedy: Add the hevel-family disclosure for this row's own closing verse oshb:Eccl.6.2 (זֶ֥ה הֶ֛בֶל) to device_notes/observed_substrate_signals, naming eccl_device_inventory.json hevel_refrain by_chapter.6 = 5, matching the symmetry already given by sibling row p02-004 at its own hevel site (oshb:Eccl.5.9). Test: confirm every chapter-6 hevel_refrain member is named across its owning row (symmetry sweep), per the standing SYMMETRY-completion rule.

rulings.challenge_claim: Two of the row's three front-seam grounds fail: a chapter break is tier-4 metadata that is never boundary evidence, and the claimed first-person-to-third-person shift runs the opposite way at the actual seam; additionally the case-report formula match ships without its tier, and two paseq segs (one inside the row's own span) go undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: TIER-4 RULE VIOLATION: the row's boundary_rationale lists "a chapter break" as one of three grounds that together "mark web:Eccl.6.1 as its own new case," and strongest_rejected_alternative repeats "the chapter boundary ... argue for a fresh row." Chapter/verse numbers are tier-4 metadata, never boundary evidence under the campaign's own standing rule (book strategy Sec.4 / TOOLKIT.md Standing rules) -- this ground must be struck, not re-weighted; confirmed by direct re-read of the row's own text, no byte dispute possible on the rule's applicability. PERSON-SHIFT INVERTED: independently re-derived from bytes -- oshb:Eccl.5.18 (= web:Eccl.5.19) opens גַּ֣ם כָּֽל הָאָדָ֡ם ("also, every man...") and oshb:Eccl.5.19 (= web:Eccl.5.20) carries יִזְכֹּ֖ר ("he will remember," 3ms) -- the PRECEDING row's own closing verses are THIRD person throughout. This row's own OPENING verse, oshb:Eccl.6.1, carries רָאִ֖יתִי ("I have seen," 1cs) -- FIRST person. The third-person scenario begins only at אִ֣ישׁ (oshb:Eccl.6.2), inside this row. The seam therefore runs third-person (preceding row's close) into first-person (this row's own opening), the reverse of the row's stated "shift from first-person testimony to a third-person...scenario" used as a front-seam ground; even read charitably as an internal (6:1-to-6:2) shift rather than a seam-crossing one, it is misapplied among the row's three stated grounds "for" separating this row from the earlier verse. TIER-UNLABELLED FORMULA MATCH: יֵ֣שׁ רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ (oshb:Eccl.6.1) is NOT byte-identical to יֵ֚שׁ רָעָ֣ה חוֹלָ֔ה רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ (oshb:Eccl.5.12 = web:Eccl.5.13) -- חוֹלָ֔ה is absent from 6.1 and אֲשֶׁ֥ר is inserted, with different accentuation on the opening two words (יֵ֣שׁ רָעָ֔ה vs יֵ֚שׁ רָעָ֣ה); confirmed by direct word-index comparison. The tail רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ IS byte-identical between the two verses (also confirmed directly); the row's "matching the formula" claim does not distinguish the byte-identical tail from the skeleton-only-matching opener, a TIER/ORDINAL DISCIPLINE gap. DISCLOSURE GAPS: pmarks_Eccl.json records a paseq seg at Eccl.6.2 (MT, confirmed count 1) -- INSIDE this row's own span -- and a second at Eccl.6.3 (MT, confirmed count 1) immediately across the rear seam; neither is mentioned anywhere in the row. oshb:Eccl.6.2 also carries the hevel refrain (זֶ֥ה הֶ֛בֶל, byte tier, an inventory verse per by_chapter.6=5) -- the same gap LF's convergent item on this row identifies independently -- while the row's observed_substrate_signals names only the under-the-sun inventory. VERIFIED CORRECT (not defects): oshb:Eccl.6.1 is a genuine tachat_hashemesh site; ch-6 refs need no dual qualifier (identity outside the offset zone); the cross-seam give-power antithesis with oshb:Eccl.5.18 is disclosed, not suppressed.
rulings.remedy: (1) Strike "a chapter break" as a stated ground from both boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative; the case-report opening formula and the person/reference-shift texture are the two grounds that actually carry weight. (2) Correct the person-shift claim to state precisely: the preceding verses (oshb:Eccl.5.18-Eccl.5.19) end third-person; this row's own opening verse (oshb:Eccl.6.1) is first-person report voice; the shift to third-person "a man..." occurs internally within this row at oshb:Eccl.6.2, not as a front-seam transition from a first-person preceding unit. (3) Tier-label the formula-match claim: disclose that the report-verb-and-refrain tail (רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ) is byte-identical between oshb:Eccl.5.12 and oshb:Eccl.6.1, while the two-word opener matches only at skeleton tier (oshb:Eccl.6.1 inserts אֲשֶׁ֥ר and omits חוֹלָ֔ה relative to oshb:Eccl.5.12). (4) Add the paseq disclosure for the seg inside this row's own span (oshb:Eccl.6.2) and the one immediately across its rear seam (oshb:Eccl.6.3), per pmarks_Eccl.json. (5) Add the hevel disclosure at oshb:Eccl.6.2 per LF's convergent item. Test: collate.py byte-tier re-check of the case-report-opener quote against both cited tiers; confirm boundary_rationale no longer lists chapter/verse numbers as a warrant; symmetry check confirming both paseq segs and the hevel site are now named.
